Every watery extension and foam edge must remain visibly attached to its body. No detached droplets, particles, spray specks, bubbles, projectiles, ground shadows or fragments. This is a floating magic water creature, never a person in a water costume. Painted 2D, no 3D rendering.

EXACT LAYOUT: TWENTY-FOUR separate complete bodies in EIGHT equal columns and THREE equal rows, perfectly regular cells. One full connected creature centered in each cell, whole silhouette including attacking water-arm reach at MOST 40-45% of cell width, at most 65% of cell height. Generous clear transparent padding all sides; at least 60 image pixels between rows and wide horizontal gutters. Every body complete and safe from clipping or touching its neighbors. No labels, numbers, guides, borders or writing.

ALL THREE ROWS use directions in this exact column order: 1 E true right-facing side profile; 2 SE front-right three-quarter; 3 S straight front; 4 SW front-left three-quarter; 5 W true left-facing side profile; 6 NW back-left three-quarter; 7 N straight back; 8 NE back-right three-quarter. Front views show the dark head-front recess and chest; side views show an actual side volume and leading front edge pointing right/left; rear views show rear water head/shoulders/torso surfaces and NEVER retain a front face or chest. All8 are independently drawn genuine angles, no mirroring or flat front stuck sideways.

ROW 1 = MAGIC ATTACK WINDUP / GATHER: both elbows deeply flex and water hands curl toward the front of chest, head and shoulders draw back slightly. The water in the attached arms thickens as if gathering power. Keep all water attached; no detached orb or effect. Body is poised and lower vortex coils tighter.
ROW 2 = MAGIC ATTACK RELEASE / HIT MOMENT: one thick watery forearm and attached hand sweep/extend firmly FORWARD along the exact facing direction, the other elbow opens forward in support, torso leans toward release. E reaches image RIGHT; SE down-right; S down/toward viewer; SW down-left; W image LEFT; NW up-left/away; N up/away; NE up-right/away. The attacking extension is part of the same attached water arm, with continuous shoulder, upper arm, elbow, forearm and water-hand connection. No weapon and NO free projectile. Retain a coherent recognizable torso and vortex. Ensure sufficient negative space around the reach inside the cell.
ROW 3 = MAGIC ATTACK RECOVERY: releasing elbow bends back down toward side, opposite arm counterbalances at a visibly different height, torso returns toward upright, lower vortex unwinds and broadens toward its normal contour. This differs from both gather and release, with actual arm articulation and water-body deformation. Do not repeat the idle still or reuse a merely translated attack pose.

Stable original character identity and proportions, exact direction per column throughout all phases, physically continuous fluid torso and limbs, lower vortex tip grounded consistently on a shared row baseline. All24 poses must be distinct actual articulated states, every complete body separated on true transparent alpha, no empty frames, detached water fragments, copied/mirrored stills, clipping or 3D assets.

ROW1 = HIT A, STRUCK RECOIL: upper torso jerks AWAY from the facing direction, shoulders twist backward and upward, one elbow rises defensively and the other water arm curls inward. Vortex base braces wider, still continuously attached. Clear hit reaction distinct from idle.

ROW5 = DEATH C, FINAL VERY LOW FLATTENED WATER BODY: the creature is visibly settled on the ground as a compact LOW PUDDLE / FLATTENED WHIRLPOOL mound, only about one-quarter of normal body height. Foamy remnants of the water head/shoulders and curled attached arms blend into one continuous flattened blue water mass. The form and attached remnants indicate each column's facing orientation but no standing full-height torso remains. The entire final puddle remains one connected substantial visible sprite, never empty/transparent and never scattered droplets. Its bottom rests exactly on the same ground baseline as earlier phases in that column. Keep flattened width within40-45%cellwidth so clear gutters survive.

Every phase needs actual changes of shoulder/elbow articulation, torso curvature and whirlpool geometry. Preserve fluid body connections, original water colors/style, source identity and per-column direction. Do not substitute translated, copied, mirrored or recolored stills, free particles, missing frames or disconnected limbs. All20 bodies separated, complete, original pixels of the generated output left intact for exact alpha-bounded sprite regions.
